title: Molecular tension microscopy of the LINC complex in live cells
protocol: Detach cells from a culture flask (T25 flask).
Prepare a new T25 flask containing 4.5 mL of fresh DMEM and place it into the incubator.
Aspirate old medium with a Pasteur pipette.
Wash once with 1 mL of PBS (Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ free) and gently swirl to dilute remaining DMEM and cell debris.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Add 1 mL of Trypsin-EDTA solution to the cell culture flask and swirl to cover the cells.
Incubate about 10 min for cells to detach from the surface and each other.
Gently shake the flask to facilitate cell detachment.
Visually assess cell detachment using an inverted phase-contrast microscope.
Collect detached cells: Add 4 mL of cell culture medium to stop trypsin enzymatic reaction, gently pipette up and down to help cell detachment, and collect all the cell suspension.
Transfer 1:10 of the volume (0.5 mL) into the new flask and put back in the incubator for future experiments.
Transfer the remaining volume (4.5 mL) of the old flask to a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Pellet cells by centrifugation at 60-125 g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant and gently resuspend the pellet in 3 mL of imaging medium (stock cell suspension).
Seed cells on coverslips in imaging medium.
Count cells with a hematocytometer or equivalent device.
Dilute stock cell suspension in imaging medium at 5 × 10⁴ cell/mL.
Rinse collagen-coated coverslips with PBS.
Rinse collagen-coated coverslips again with imaging medium to remove acid residues.
Transfer 1.5 mL of the 5 × 10^4 cell/mL suspension into each well of the 2-well chambered coverslip.
Pipette up and down twice in the well to facilitate homogeneous seeding and avoid cell aggregation at the center.
Incubate the cells for at least 12 hours to allow for cell attachment.
Transfect cells just after cell attachment, at least one hour after seeding.
Use two wells of a coverslip for nesprin tension sensor (CB).
Use two wells of another coverslip for its control (CH mutant).
Use two wells of a last coverslip for FRET standards (5AA and TRAF).
Prepare a 1.5 mL tube with 100 μL FluoroBrite medium without serum.
Pipette 1 μg DNA into the prepared tube and vortex for 10 seconds.
Briefly vortex the transfection reagent and add 2 μL to the diluted DNA.
Mix immediately by vortexing for 10 seconds.
Incubate the mixture at 18°C–25°C for 15 minutes.
Prepare another 1.5 mL tube with 900 μL of imaging medium.
Add 100 μL of the DNA/lipid particles mixture to the second tube.
Flick the tube to homogenously distribute DNA/lipid particles.
Gently aspirate and discard the imaging medium from the well using a micropipette and filter tip.
Add 1 mL of the tube prepared in step 4f to the well.
Incubate the cells at 37°C (5% CO2) for 4 hours.
Aspirate and discard the medium from the transfected well using a micropipette and filter tip.
Add 1 mL of imaging medium to the well.
Incubate the cells at 37°C (5% CO2) for at least 24 hours (up to 48 hours).
Turn on the microscope.
Set the incubation parameters to 37°C and 5% CO2, about 1 hour before imaging.
Select the 63×/1.4NA Plan-Apochromat Oil objective and appropriate immersion oil.
Select an appropriate Dichroic mirror for exciting GFP protein.
Prepare 500 μL of pre-warmed imaging medium per condition, at 4× final concentration.
Remove 250 μL from each well using a micropipette with filter tips.
Add 250 μL of the prepared imaging medium to each well.
Allow cells to rest for 15 minutes in the cell culture incubator.
Place imaging coverslip with cells on the microscope stage.
Add mineral oil on top of the imaging medium to prevent evaporation.
Visualize fluorescent cells using epifluorescence microscopy.
Slowly bring cells into focus without damaging the glass bottom dish.
Verify that cells are transfected and construct expression is at the expected location.
Choose cells with a good signal-to-noise ratio for image acquisition.
Select lambda mode and set the acquisition range from 471 nm to 562 nm with a spectral resolution of 9.0 nm on the spectral channel (ChS).
Set the excitation beam splitter MBS458.
Use unidirectional, 2× line averaging at speed 7 for a 1024 × 1024 pixels² frame corresponding to a real size of 135 × 135 μm² with pixel size 0.13 × 0.13 μm².
Set the power of the 458 nm excitation laser to about 70%.
Use a pinhole and detector parameters typical for regular scanning confocal imaging, typically a 49.4 μm (1 Airy Unit) pinhole.
Start the acquisition.
Save your acquisition and repeat on another field of view as desired.
Choose an objective with the highest numerical aperture, typically 1.4 for standard objectives, to maximize resolution and signal intensity.
Beware of photo-bleaching by keeping epifluorescence light source and laser low and minimizing exposure time before acquisition.
Select the multichannel ZEISS .lsm or .czi file for analysis.
Choose one of the two image analysis workflows: ‘Nuclei’ or ‘Whole cell’ option.
Insert background values manually in Donor/Acceptor channel numeric fields if desired.
Open the selected file and check its dimensions.
Select a series to analyze from multiple positions using the slider.
Create a folder named ‘[filename(without extension)]+_S+[selected series number]’ for data storage.
Display the Maximum Intensity Projection (MIP) of the multichannel stack.
Manually select a rectangular ROI containing the fluorescent protein signal.
Display the mean intensity profile through the multichannel image.
Select channels corresponding to donor and acceptor intensity maxima.
Apply a Gaussian filter with a radius of 2 pixels to both selected channels.
Assign NaN value to saturated and 0-value pixels.
Manually select a line ROI in the darkest area of the image using the freehand line tool.
Measure the mean intensity value within the ROI for each channel.
Subtract the measured background intensity from the whole image for each channel.
Save each background-subtracted channel in the ‘analyzed data’ folder created in task 1, labeling them as 'c1' (donor) and 'c2' (acceptor).
Select min and max intensity values of pixels for FRET index display.
Generate thresholded donor and acceptor images with selected pixel values retained, others set to NaN.
Apply formula FRET index (in %) = 100 × IFRET / (IFRET + IDonor) to each non-NaN pixel.
Display an image where every selected pixel shows a FRET index value in % using ‘Fire’ color map.
Save the resulting image as ‘FRET index (%).tif’.
Create a single row Result Table called ‘Mean FRET index (%)’ with area, mean FRET index, and standard deviation.
Generate a FRET index image (in %) from the background-corrected donor and acceptor images using the formula from step 19 of ‘Whole cell’ workflow.
Save the resulting image as ‘FRET index (%).tif’.
Manually point with the multi-point selection tool all nuclei in the MIP image.
Save the coordinates of these markers as a set of ROIs under the name ‘RoiSet_Markers.zip’.
Segment all selected regions using the Marker-controlled Watershed plugin from the MorphoLibJ library.
Select background regions in the segmented image using the multi-point selection tool.
Merge selected background regions with nucleus regions touching the border using the 'Merge Label and Kill border' function from MorphoLibJ library.
Save the resulting image as 'LabelBordersRGB.tif' with a Jet color map and white background.
Interpolate labeled nuclei within closed polygon ROIs, spacing points one pixel apart by applying a 3-point running average.
Discard polygons with less than 10 points.
Save the set of resulting ROIs as 'RoiSet_NucleiContour.zip'.
Generate a 3-pixels-thick band from each ROI.
Save the set of resulting ROIs as 'RoiSet_NucleiBand.zip'.
Create a result table for each pixel within the band of each nucleus contour, including columns for IObject, Iname, IcontourPoints, PointX, PointY, and FRET index (%).
Save the table as 'ContourMeasurements.csv'.
Set all pixels excluded from the 3-pixels thick nucleus contour to NaN in the FRET index image obtained previously.
